item.title: Nancy Mace has a message for the libs who were triggered by her SEC Saturday, Caleb Williams memes & Brady!
item.description: Nancy Mace fired back at critics over her "Go Cocks!" South Carolina football post, while Caleb Williams' injury reaction set the internet ablaze.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Don't look now, but we're embarking on the final full week of September. I know. Doesn't seem possible, but here we are.

It's why we have to cherish every single one of these fall weekends, folks. They take so long to get here, and then you look up and we're already into Week 4 of the college football season.

Blink, and we'll be ringing doorbells for candy. Blink again, and we'll be carving turkeys.

SYDNEY THOMAS MOCKS LANE KIFFIN AFTER LOSS WITH BRUTAL HALLOWEEN COSTUME IDEA, LSU FANS FIGHT & NATE'S SHORTS

Don't let a single day go to waste. We're in the best time of year.

Welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where Nancy Mace sends her haters a stern message after they got all riled up over her attending Saturday's South Carolina game.

"Go Cocks!"

What else? I've got Caleb Williams memes flooding the internet after yesterday's wild injury (and reaction), Tom Brady ruffled some feathers with his language on yesterday's broadcast (silly), and I think college football really separated itself from the NFL this weekend.

I assume it'll swing back and forth throughout the season, but it was pretty stark yesterday. I'll explain.

OK, grab you whatever it was Patrick Mahomes was slugging back before last night's OT win, and settle in for a Monday 'Cap!

No, it wasn't anything nefarious. That little cocktail would be pickle juice — a staple for any athlete. My wife loves pickle juice. I despise it.

I love pickles. Can't stand pickle juice. People just drink that stuff out of the jar. It's unfathomable to me.

But, to each their own. We don't judge here. (We do).

Anyway, let's get this class going. It's a Monday, and the official last day of summer given the fall equinox begins tomorrow. We're back in the 80s pretty consistently here in Florida, so it's almost sweater weather!

First up today? Nancy Mace triggering the left with her SEC video over the weekend, and then sending the haters a strongly worded message after the dust settled:

"I've had some time to reflect on my attendance at a college football game last night and then had the nerve to tweet about it," Mace says, referring to the internet melting down her "Go Cocks!" caption.

"So this post goes out to all the liberals, libtards, socialists, leftists, and trolls that don't think women should attend football games or cheer for their team with their college football chant. I want you to know that I've unpacked your lived experiences and I've centered your truth and your feelings. Your feelings are valid. But despite all of that, I'm unburdened by what has been.

"And so I'm going to attend — I've decided I'm going to attend the next football game and enjoy the hell out of it."

SEC TEAMS WENT 16-0 IN WEEK 1, IS THE CONFERENCE BACK ON TOP OF COLLEGE FOOTBALL WORLD?

It just means more in the SEC, baby! Get 'em, Nancy. Don't let the haters win this round. "Go Cocks!" has been South Carolina's calling card forever now. You can't drive down the street in Columbia without seeing it.

The Gamecocks lost to Miss. State, 41-34, for what it's worth. Good game, though. Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor may be the best quarterback in college football. He feels like someone who won't be a Bulldog next season, sadly.

Next? Speaking of players who can sling the rock, Caleb Williams is all over the internet today. He went down with what appeared to be a season-ending injury late in Sunday's game against Minnesota, and it basically took the jaws of life to get him off the field and into the locker room.

Turns out, he just pulled a hammy.

Naturally, his reaction to the injury is getting ruthlessly mocked:

Amazing.

Look, I'm not here to tell you a hamstring strain doesn't hurt. It does. We also don't yet know how severe it is. It's never great when muscles get yanked off the bone.

But ... I legitimately thought Caleb Williams suffered a career-ending injury with his reaction. I've never seen a player yell or scream like that. Watching them try to walk him off the field was wild. I thought there was a real chance they were gonna have to call in the stretcher.

I figured we'd seen the last of him until next September ...

And then it came out last night that it was a hamstring injury. Not ACL. Not achilles. No broken bones. Hamstring.

He's not even being ruled out for next WEEK, according to Tom Pelissero! Amazing.

I like Caleb Williams, by the way. I think he's a superstar quarterback. Unfortunately, that meme will now be used for the rest of eternity.

As is life on the internet. It's a tough world out there.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Monday class into a big Monday night. Speaking of the internet jumping all over someone ...

Are people really mad at Tom Brady for saying "piss missile" on live TV? Is that not allowed? Am I got crazy? I've seen people whining on social media today because Brady cussed and said "piss" during the broadcast.

Give me a break. Everyone was mad at Tom two years ago because he was too robotic and reserved in the booth. Now we're mad at him for this? And no, I'm not just saying this because Brady is a Fox teammate. I'm saying it because it's NUTS how mad we get at the silliest things nowadays.

That ball from Dak WAS a piss missile! Get over it.

Finally, on the way out, I do have a question I'd like to leave for the class ...

I saw that post this morning and it really spoke to me.

NFL vs. College football ... who ya got? After this weekend, I think it's pretty clear college football is just better at the moment. And I'm a HUGE NFL guy. It's always been my No. 1 sport. Probably still is ...

But the gap is getting pretty small. I don't know how you can watch Ole Miss-LSU Saturday night, and then go into yesterday's 1 p.m. slate of games, and not feel a difference.

College football Saturdays are just so much better. Perhaps it's because of the day itself, which is fair. We all prefer Saturdays over Sundays. Can't fault the NFL for that.

But beyond that, the atmosphere is just better. The pregame shows. The hype. The crowds. The storylines. Most of all, college football almost always delivers.

LSU-Ole Miss delivered Saturday night. Even with all the hype, the game somehow still delivered.

Maybe this is simply recency bias on my part given yesterday's NFL slate was pretty awful. But I do think the difference was night and day this weekend.

Something to monitor.

OK, that's it for today. Happy last day of summer to all who celebrate.

Let's have a big week.

NFL or college? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

item.title: Georgia school district defends pulling 'sexually explicit' book depicting child rape amid 'censorship' claims
item.description: Cobb County removed Toni Morrison's "The Bluest Eye" over graphic child rape depictions, but PEN America warns that book "censorship" is a slippery slope.
item.content:encoded:
A Georgia school district has removed Toni Morrison’s "The Bluest Eye" from its public school libraries, citing graphic depictions of child rape and incest in the award-winning novel.

The book joins over 30 other titles removed by Cobb County, Georgia’s second-largest school district, since 2023 as part of an effort to remove sexually explicit material from K-12 media centers.

District leaders say the move is intended to protect students and give parents more control over what their kids are exposed to, while free-speech advocates argue the removal amounts to censorship and limits students’ access to literature.

"We're no more banning the book than we are banning rated-R movies. It's just that we are removing those with sexually explicit content and allowing our parents to make those decisions for their families," Cobb County Superintendent Chris Ragsdale told Fox News Digital.

OREGON SCHOOL COUNSELOR FACES BACKLASH OVER 'CHOSEN FAMILY' BOOK FOR YOUTHS

Ragsdale said district colleagues brought the book to his attention because of concerns about excerpts dealing with sexual topics. At a board meeting, Ragsdale read aloud one explicit passage that depicts the rape of an 11-year-old girl by her father.

"Both as a father and as a superintendent, I think about a parent having to explain to their sixth-grade daughter after she encounters explicit descriptions of child incest and rape in a book provided at school, without parents' knowledge," Ragsdale said in the book removal announcement posted online.

"As the superintendent responsible for the instruction of 100,000 students, I do not have the luxury of making that decision for other parents and their children," he added.

The district announced the book would join dozens of others removed from school shelves, including the popular "A Court of Thorns and Roses" series, "The Perks of Being a Wallflower," "Me, Earl, and the Dying Girl," and "Thirteen Reasons Why." The latter was eventually adapted into a Netflix series about a high school girl who dies by suicide.

ALASKA STATE FAIR BARS PARENTAL RIGHTS GROUP DUE TO 'EXTREMIST' GROUP DESIGNATION BY FAR-LEFT ORGANIZATION

District officials said other works by Toni Morrison remain available in Cobb County schools. The district says its removals target books containing sexually explicit passages.

Ragsdale acknowledged the author’s award-winning status, but argued that awards do not mean a book belongs in every K-12 school library. He said books containing sexually explicit material are subject to a separate administrative review process, rather than Georgia’s standard process for parent challenges.

The superintendent rejected the characterization of the district’s actions as book banning or censorship.

"And there's not a single classroom in our school district that will show a rated R movie during class to students," Ragsdale said. "Same thing for these books that contain sexually explicit material. That needs to be a parental decision made in the parents and the child's house."

"One size does not fit all. So we can't just make a cross-the-board decision for parents and expect that every parent is going to agree with that decision," Ragsdale later added. "We want the parents to be able to be empowered to make the decisions that, as parents, they should be able to make."

Parental advocacy group Moms for Liberty echoed Ragsdale’s argument, telling Fox News Digital that schools are not required to stock every book and can decide what their students have access to in the school library. 

"Schools are not required to stock every published work. They already restrict internet access, movies, and other materials for age-appropriateness," said Tina Descovich, Moms for Liberty CEO and co-founder.

"The book ‘The Bluest Eye’ went through the Cobb County School District’s review process and the process worked. The community determined that graphic descriptions of the rape and incest of a young girl in a book on shelves accessible to 11-year-old students in school, often without a parent’s knowledge or consent, is not acceptable," Descovich added.

"At the end of the day, this is about protecting students and ensuring parents are not blindsided by their child’s assigned reading list," she said.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS ‘HARD RESET’ FOR AMERICAN SCHOOLS, VOWS TO PUT PARENTS ‘BACK IN CHARGE’

Kasey Meehan, Freedom to Read Director at PEN America, criticized the decision and said Morrison’s works are often targeted using excerpts that are taken out of the context of the books as a whole.

"While that particular part of a book can be really difficult to read and to sit with and grapple with, what we continue to point to is that books are not harmful, censorship is," Meehan told Fox News Digital.

"So what we hear time and time again is that books like ‘The Bluest Eye’ and other books that talk about sex, talk about consensual sex, as well as talk about violence and sexual experiences, they help young people gain really profound and necessary literacy around what consent is, what harm is and how to be in relationships that are mutually loving," she later added.

Meehan also challenged the district’s argument regarding parental choice, saying district-wide decisions restrict access to books for every student, regardless of age or interest.

"Increasingly, we've seen the way in which state laws or politicians or even broadly, district administrators are making decisions that affect the access of books for every student in the district, regardless of age, regardless of interest," Meehan said.

"I think we often point to that making these broad, sweeping decisions that restrict access to titles, restrict the freedom to read for every student in that district," she said. "[It] undercuts the professional expertise of educators and librarians who see, of course, the literary merit and value in having that book accessible for young readers."

Meehan also warned that what may begin with the removal of a single book could expand to other titles.

"While it may seem like it's one book, censorship is a slippery slope, and it never actually ends with just one book or one title," Meehan said. "Oftentimes, districts that ban one book then continue to remove all kinds of literature from school."

item.title: White House won't back down as attorney predicts how Trump's latest press tussle will play out in court
item.description: A First Amendment attorney predicts Trump's White House ban on CNN, Politico and MS NOW will fail in court, calling the action blatantly unconstitutional.
item.content:encoded:
An attorney at a nonprofit that defends the First Amendment doesn't think President Donald Trump will come out on top in a legal battle with three media outlets he banned from the White House.

But after announcing on Friday his ban of CNN, MS NOW and Politico — and the resulting lawsuit against him — the White House told Fox News Digital that Trump isn't backing down.

"I think the Trump administration will not fare well in court because its action here is blatantly unconstitutional," predicted Aaron Terr, the director of public advocacy at the Philadelphia-based Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression (FIRE).

Trump took to TRUTH Social on Friday to announce that employees with the three major media outlets will be banned from White House grounds over "reporting FAKE NEWS. He said they "shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States."

DISNEY SUES FCC OVER ‘RETALIATORY CAMPAIGN AGAINST ABC,’ SEEKS TO BLOCK EARLY RENEWAL PROCEEDINGS

Terr says that what media outlets report is not at issue.

"There's settled precedent that when the White House opens its doors to the press, which it has done, the First Amendment walks in too," Terr said. "So that means the administration can't ban reporters from the White House grounds just because it doesn't like their point of view or thinks their coverage is too negative or critical, and the president in his statements has been crystal clear that this was the exact reason that he banned CNN, MSN, and ... Politico from the entire White House grounds."

Reporters and cameramen with the outlets removed their gear and set up on Pennsylvania Ave. over the weekend and this week continued to film live hits from across the street rather than from their usual spots on White House grounds.

In response to Terr's assessment, the White House remained defiant about the ban.

"The Fake News has no place demanding a spot in the President’s Oval Office," the White House said. "The lies they smear are a disservice to the American public and tear at the very fabric of our Democracy. They’re completely capable of reporting from directly outside."

CNN FIRES BACK AT TRUMP WHITE HOUSE OVER ATTACKS ON REPORTER, CALLS THEM 'BENEATH THE OFFICE'

Monday morning, the three news outlets filed a lawsuit against Trump seeking an injunction that would halt the president's ban temporarily, and asking the court to immediately order the restoration of the media members' White House credentials.

CNN was scheduled for White House television pool coverage on Monday. Fox News Media, ABC News, CBS News and NBC News, the other press pool networks, announced in a joint statement that they would not take CNN's place.

"The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting," the pool members said in a joint statement.

Additionally, White House Correspondents' Association (WHCA) President Jacqui Heinrich of Fox News, released a statement expressing the organization's support of the outlets.

"Today’s action revoking access for journalists from CNN, POLITICO, and MSNOW violates the First Amendment," she wrote. "The implications extend beyond these organizations: a standard used to exclude one news outlet because of its coverage could be applied to any outlet in the future."

"The American people, through a free and independent press, must be able to scrutinize those elected to power, regardless of whether government officials view it favorably," she continued. "The WHCA calls on the administration to immediately restore our colleagues’ access."

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION SUBPOENAS NY TIMES JOURNALISTS IN GRAND JURY LEAK PROBE TIED TO AIR FORCE ONE REPORT

Terr said that while nobody has a First Amendment right to report from the White House, he said court precedent established that once a media outlet gains access to the White House, that access cannot be revoked for ideological reasons.

"The principle here is that once the government provides access, it then can't condition that access on whether you're expressing a viewpoint that the government agrees with," he said. "It's a broader First Amendment principle that the government cannot retaliate against Americans for protected speech, and that includes revoking news outlets' access to a space open to the press just because the president doesn't like the actual or perceived slant of their report."

Terr noted that while there can be bias in media, the alternative of government-controlled media could result in a much worse outcome.

"The First Amendment is designed to prevent exactly that type of government control over the flow of information in a free society," he said. "The First Amendment guarantees that reporters are free to cover the news in a way that they think is best, and it's up to the American public to hear what they have to say and decide whether or not to trust them and their coverage of the government and other issues in our society."

item.title: Kyler Murray clears concussion protocol and will start for Vikings against Tampa Bay Buccaneers
item.description: Kyler Murray cleared the NFL concussion protocol and will start Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after missing the Chicago Bears game.
item.content:encoded:
Kyler Murray is back for the Minnesota Vikings.

Coach Kevin O'Connell announced Monday afternoon that the quarterback has cleared the NFL concussion protocol and will start on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Murray missed Sunday's game against the Chicago Bears because he was knocked out of the Week 1 game against the Green Bay Packers.

KYLER MURRAY KNOCKED OUT OF VIKINGS DEBUT AFTER FOREARM TO THE HELMET AND BLOW TO NECK BY TWO PACKERS

The hit was ugly, and although Murray walked to the locker room and seemed totally responsive in the hours afterward, he was placed in the NFL concussion protocol.

Murray, who won the starting job in training camp against J.J. McCarthy, was thus subjected to testing by independent physicians to determine his status.

And while that happened, Carson Wentz directed a comeback win against the Packers and then a victory over the Bears on Sunday.

MINNESOTA VIKINGS SURPRISINGLY DEMOTE FORMER FIRST-ROUND PICK JJ MCCARTHY TO THIRD STRING

The Vikings lead the NFC North with a 2-0 record.

Sunday's victory was not exactly an offensive explosion, which might explain why O'Connell didn't hesitate in handing the starting job back to Murray.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Wentz completed 11 of 20 passes for a modest 143 without a touchdown or interception in the 9-3 victory over the Bears.

The time Wentz played in his place was not wasted by Murray, according to O'Connell.

VIKINGS QUARTERBACK BATTLE MEETS EXPECTED END AS KYLER MURRAY BEATS OUT JJ MCCARTHY FOR STARTING JOB

"I think the starting point is he's just watched Carson really function in a way that there wasn't, Carson wasn't, you know, doing crazy things," O'Connell said. "He was just protecting the football, making good decisions, making some big-time throws when he could, and running the show.

"And and I think [Murray] saw some plays get made. I think he saw our team play totally connected and complimentary of all of the other two phases and what that can do for the Minnesota Vikings on a Sunday."
